author: Elastic
attributes.description: Detects a shell `rm` of a path under `/var/log` or of a `*.log` name. Those files hold shell commands, authentication, and hostd activity. Removing them takes away the record of what changed on the host.
false_positives: An administrator deletes a rotated log under `/var/log` during a documented maintenance window. Confirm the path and the change ticket.
attributes.name: ESXi Host Logs Deleted with rm
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating ESXi Host Logs Deleted with rm

shell.log records the typed command. The rule matches a line that contains rm together with a /var/log/ path or a *.log name, such as [root]: rm -f /var/log/hostd.log or [root]: rm *.log.

#### Possible investigation steps

- Read message and note the path that was deleted.
- On the host, list /var/log and see which files are missing, including shell.log, auth.log, and hostd.log.
- Review account changes, firewall changes, and VM power events from the same session that are still in the index.

### False positive analysis

Deleting one rotated log during maintenance can be expected. rm *.log removes every log name in the current directory and should be explained by a ticket.

### Response and remediation

- If the delete was not approved, isolate the host and preserve any remaining logs before they rotate.
- Rotate credentials used in that shell session.
- Confirm remote syslog still has a copy of the deleted host logs.
attributes.query: data_stream.dataset:vsphere.log and event.module:vsphere and message:(rm and ("*.log" or "/var/log/*"))
attributes.setup:
## Setup

This rule requires ESXi host logs collected by the Elastic vSphere integration: https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations/vsphere

subtechnique.name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
